newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen wobbly, to test higher level.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen wobbly, to test higher level.

text.p: Singapore shares looked ripe to test higher levels on Wednesday after a period of consolidation, but investors are still sidelined, dealers said.
Institutions are selectively buying blue chip stocks, such as banks and property counters, but many are cautious ahead of the presentation of Singapore's budget in parliament on July 11.
"We're waiting to see what snatches of goodies they will throw our way or will they tighten the knot a little more," one broker said, noting some speculation about tax cuts.
On Tuesday, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed 6.67 points lower at 1,981.28. Volume was a weak 84 million shares with losers outpacing gainers 194 to 93.
Dealers said the focus on Hong Kong and China this week and downgrading of regional stocks by investment houses was likely to stifle activity somewhat.
Wall Street's rise overnight could be a countering boost. The Dow Jones industrial average ended 49.54 points higher at 7,722.33.
